title: Feature request: add custom mapping in .desktop file for audio stream
line: Apps whose sound is played by a separate program, like MPD frontends, can now get the task manager's audio indicator and volume controls through a .desktop key.
explanation: The task manager matches audio streams to windows by portal app id, then by process id (or parent process id), then by application name. A frontend such as Cantata talks to MPD, which plays the sound from its own process under the name "Music Player Daemon", so none of those match and the frontend's task never gets the audio indicator, mute or volume slider. The task manager now reads an X-KDE-AudioStreamAppNames list from the app's .desktop file and, when no stream matches the window's process, uses the streams whose application name is in that list.

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: let apps name their audio streams in .desktop files

Apps like MPD frontends don't play audio themselves, so their window
can't be matched to the stream and gets no volume controls. They can
now list the stream's app names in X-KDE-AudioStreamAppNames instead.

BUG: 511921

media.caption: Info Center's .desktop file names the "Music Player Daemon" stream (playing from another process): no audio icon, no volume slider
Same setup: the task shows the audio icon and its tooltip has the stream's volume slider

reviews.text: Supporting a .desktop key (X-KDE-AudioStreamAppNames) for apps whose audio is played by a separate daemon like MPD directly addresses the feature request and works in the before/after verification. However, binding audioStreamAppNames directly on every Task.qml delegate causes synchronous KDesktopFile disk I/O on the plasmashell GUI thread for every pinned launcher and window even when no audio is playing. Also, using `else if` skips the existing appName fallback when the key is set but the named stream is not active.
changes: Avoid synchronous KDesktopFile disk reads for every task delegate (especially pinned launchers where !task.isWindow and when no streams are active): only resolve X-KDE-AudioStreamAppNames lazily for windows when audio stream matching actually falls past appId/PID lookup, and cache results per launcherUrl in Backend.

Change the `else if (task.audioStreamAppNames.length)` branch in Task.qml to a sequential `if (!streams.length && ...)` check before the existing `streamsForAppName(model.AppName)` fallback so configuring the key does not suppress normal fallback matching when the external stream isn't playing.
Document the new X-KDE-AudioStreamAppNames .desktop key format (semicolon-separated XDG list matched against PulseAudio/PipeWire application.name) in code/docs.

reviews.text: Implements exactly what the reporter asked for: a .desktop key (X-KDE-AudioStreamAppNames) that maps a frontend's task to streams with another application.name, used only after portal-id and PID matching fail, so existing matching is untouched. The change is small, reuses the existing Backend .desktop-reading pattern and PulseAudio.findStreamsFn, and the before/after screenshots plus the pactl mute/volume check prove it. Nitpick: the property reads and parses the .desktop file eagerly for every task delegate (launchers included); computing it lazily inside updateAudioStreams only when the PID match fails would avoid that I/O, and the key name should be mentioned in the MR so maintainers can bikeshed it.
